proposed_fix.description: Verify emailservice CPU limits/requests against actual usage and, if throttling is confirmed, raise the container's CPU limit in a reversible, human-approved change.
steps: Check whether emailservice pods are being CPU throttled (e.g., container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total) and compare current CPU usage to configured requests and limits.
Check emailservice pod health and recent restarts or deploys to understand why inbound calls are failing (E2 shows ~98% inbound errors).
Check the node kernel version and node CPU headroom where emailservice runs (R3).

If throttling is confirmed and the app is behaving erratically (inbound errors per E2), propose a modest increase to the emailservice container CPU limit only, leaving requests unchanged (R3), and get on-call approval before applying.
After applying, watch emailservice_cpu and inbound error rate for several minutes to confirm recovery.
preconditions: Confirm throttling or CPU saturation actually exists for emailservice; R1 says throttling alone is informational.
Confirm the inbound errors in E2 are not caused by an upstream or caller-side problem or a bad deploy.
Confirm the node has spare CPU capacity to honor a higher limit.
Record the current deployment manifest/limits so they can be restored.
proposed_fix.rollback: Revert the emailservice deployment to the previously recorded CPU limit (e.g., kubectl rollout undo or re-apply the saved manifest) and confirm pods return to the prior spec.
